facts.fact: PO-RALG directive of 31 January 2023 told local government authorities to install TAUSI by 31 March 2023, register all POS devices and stop collecting through LGRCIS.
The CAG says there is no budget for system implementation in 137 LGAs and recommends PO-RALG secure funding for the full rollout of TAUSI in all 184 LGAs.

The audit reviewed bills issued through TAUSI by LGAs for the period ended 30 June 2024; the Revenue Administration Manual it cites says taxpayer records in the billing system update automatically on payment.
The CAG says the system is designed with taxpayer databases, e-receipts and reports; it lists TZS 12.20 billion of defaulters held in LGRCIS across 26 LGAs, so LGRCIS held debtors against payers.

The CAG found 16 LGAs collected TZS 6.68 billion through LGRCIS instead of TAUSI in 2023/24 because sources such as hotel levy and building permits were not configured in TAUSI; no total is stated here.
Table 20 lists 20 LGAs with revenue collected through TAUSI but not banked in 2023/24, and 23 with LGRCIS; the count of LGAs using TAUSI is a floor.
PO-RALG implemented the TAUSI property tax module in only 47 of 184 LGAs (25.5 percent, computed from the CAG's 47 and 137), the rest relying on TANESCO collections; December 2024 reporting.
